picks.title: Anthropic's Claude Designs Leaner Quantum Circuits, Reducing Resources Needed for Key Calculations
picks.excerpt: Researchers used Claude to design more efficient quantum circuits across eight tasks, reducing estimated computing resources.
picks.rationale: Quantum slot and the newest item in the pool: an LLM designs leaner quantum circuits on eight tasks and cuts the estimated resources needed.

picks.title: Machine learning analysis of gene regulation reveals new dimension of biological variability
picks.excerpt: The FIRE tool adds a machine-learning step to long-read chromatin-accessibility mapping, scoring each accessible DNA region on maternal and paternal chromosomes for real regulatory function (study in Cell).
picks.rationale: Genomics slot: a Cell study in which ML scores each accessible DNA region separately on the maternal and paternal chromosomes, a new level of detail in gene-regulation maps.

picks.title: Fully automated testing of bulk metals paves the way for AI-driven materials development
picks.excerpt: Tohoku University and NIMS built an automated bulk-metal testing line with an AI optimizer that tunes furnace parameters, a step toward a closed-loop self-driving lab that proposes the next heat-treatment conditions itself.
picks.rationale: Materials slot: Tohoku and NIMS automate bulk-metal testing end to end, with an AI optimizer that tunes the furnace parameters. This is a new release dated three weeks after the 9-27 self-driving-lab card.

picks.title: Can AI help discover new food physics? Researchers pair AI with human expertise
picks.excerpt: Penn State's AgentXtract uses AI agents to extract food-property data from papers into an expert-verified database, which surfaced a previously unreported link between two dielectric properties across 100+ foods.
picks.rationale: Literature-mining slot: AI agents pull data from papers into a database that experts check, and that database turned up a dielectric-property link across 100+ foods that no one had reported.

picks.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
picks.excerpt: StudentSim is a research system for evaluating and improving AI tutoring tools before they are tested with learners. It models how individuals may engage with tutors, giving feedback to improve tutor performance across subjects like chess, writing, and mathematics.
picks.rationale: Learning-science slot: StudentSim simulates how learners respond so AI tutors can be tested before they reach real students. This is a new system, not commentary.
